advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Wrap the subprocess communicate loop so a TimeoutExpired kills all spawned writer/pruner processes before the test fails.
evidence: ABSENCE: no try/except around communicate and no p.kill() in a finally to reap the process pool on timeout
advisory.finding: In the regression test, `p.communicate(timeout=180)` can raise `subprocess.TimeoutExpired`, but there is no `finally`/`kill()` cleanup, so a hung writer/pruner subprocess and its remaining siblings leak as orphaned processes holding the store lock.
scenarios: A deadlocked or slow subprocess under heavy CI load causes TimeoutExpired; the test aborts leaving live subprocesses

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Have the pruner worker emit a success/prune count and assert in the test that meaningful concurrent pruning actually occurred, so a silently no-opping pruner cannot yield a false GREEN.
evidence: _prune_race_worker.py:46-52: `for _ in range(rounds): for tid in tids: try: _queue.enqueue(...); _prune_queue_events(tid, t) except BaseException: pass` — no success counter, no output
test_enrich_drain_prune_concurrency.py:96-99: pruner Popen uses `stdout=subprocess.DEVNULL` — pruner emits no signal

test_enrich_drain_prune_concurrency.py:114-118: the sole assertion checks writer swallowed_raises and disk_total == intended_total; nothing asserts the pruner ran or pruned anything, so a silently no-opping pruner yields a trivially-green pass (regression blindness for the contention precondition)
advisory.finding: The pruner subprocess produces no liveness/contention oracle: it swallows all exceptions with a bare `pass`, discards stdout, and the test never asserts that any prune actually executed (e.g. that queue events were removed or that N prune commits succeeded). If the pruner path silently no-ops in the child (import/signature drift in `_queue.enqueue`, `_queue._resolve`, or `_prune_queue_events`), contention vanishes and the test still passes GREEN with zero writes lost — a false pass that no longer exercises the prune-vs-locked-write seam the diff hardens.
scenarios: A future refactor changes `_prune_queue_events`/`_queue._resolve`/`_queue.enqueue` such that the child raises on import or early-returns; the pruner does nothing, no writes race, and the test passes though the race is no longer exercised.
advisory.suggested_fix: In the pruner branch, count successful `_prune_queue_events` calls (and/or prune commits) and `print` the total (as the writer does); capture pruner stdout in the test and assert it is > 0 (contention actually happened) alongside the zero-loss disk oracle.
